title: DW-MT321-BaseImageRegistryCas
group: DW Durable workspace volumes and handoff
clause: Content-addressed read-only base rootfs images: digest-named CAS files with atomic temp+rename writes and integrity-verified reads, plus a SurrealDB base-image registry (one row per toolchain version); bases with children are never writable

scope.summary:
GOAL: Create the storage foundation of the DW family: a host-side content-addressed store (CAS) for immutable blobs plus a SurrealDB registry of read-only base rootfs images, one registered image per toolchain version. This is the Docker-image-layer analog from research P7 rebuilt Rust-native with zero Docker/containerd/OCI dependency: the OCI descriptor/manifest layout (P11) and the cacache write discipline (P12: temp-file write, fsync, atomic rename, integrity re-verification on every read, 'never gives corrupted data') are format/shape heuristics only. Base images are what MT-322's per-workspace qcow2 delta boot disks point at via backing-file chains, so the P4 rule is absolute from day one: a base image that has children is NEVER opened for write - modifying a backing file invalidates every overlay (QEMU block-driver doc cited in P4). Everything is account/Principal-scoped from the first row: the registry table carries the same five resource-scope columns as worktree_vm_bindings (migrations/0365_worktree_vm_bindings.sql lines 17-21) and registers itself in model_lane_resource_scope_registry exactly like 0365 lines 38-40.

EXPECTED DIFF SHAPE: new module family src/backend/handshake_core/src/workspace_volumes/ (mod.rs, cas.rs, base_image_registry.rs, runtime_root.rs) wired into lib.rs; one new append-only migration (next free sequence number at implementation time, name pattern 03NN_base_image_registry.surql - WP-1's 0365 is the current tail on the feature branch); tests under src/backend/handshake_core/tests/. No adapter, protocol, or GUI changes in this MT.

DETAILED SPEC:
1. Digest type (cas.rs):
   pub struct Sha256Digest([u8; 32]);
   - Display/serde as lowercase hex with mandatory "sha256:" prefix (OCI descriptor digest shape, P11); FromStr rejects wrong prefix, wrong length, uppercase, non-hex. Ord + Hash derived so digests key BTreeMaps deterministically.
2. Runtime root resolution (runtime_root.rs):
   pub fn resolve_workspace_volumes_root() -> Result<PathBuf, WorkspaceVolumesError>
   Resolution order: explicit config value > HANDSHAKE_RUNTIME_ROOT env (trimmed, non-empty) > platform data dir fallback. HARD GUARD: the resolved root MUST NOT be inside any git repo worktree - walk ancestors and refuse (typed error WorkspaceVolumesError::RootInsideRepoWorktree) if any ancestor contains a .git file or directory. Workspace volume bytes live under the product runtime root, never inside repo worktrees. All stored paths are RELATIVE to this root (disk-agnostic per [GLOBAL-PORTABILITY]); no drive letters, no spaces in any generated file or directory name. Layout: <root>/workspace_volumes/cas/sha256/<64-hex>, <root>/workspace_volumes/cas/tmp/<uuid>.partial.
3. CAS store (cas.rs):
   pub struct HostCasStore { root: PathBuf }
   pub fn put_blob(&self, reader: impl Read) -> Result<(Sha256Digest, u64), CasError>  // stream-hash into cas/tmp/<uuid>.partial, fsync the file, atomic rename to cas/sha256/<hex>, fsync the parent directory, then set the blob file read-only
   pub fn open_verified(&self, digest: &Sha256Digest) -> Result<VerifiedBlobReader, CasError>  // reader that hashes while streaming and returns CasError::IntegrityViolation { expected, observed } at EOF on mismatch - callers structurally cannot obtain unverified full reads
   pub fn blob_path(&self, digest: &Sha256Digest) -> PathBuf; pub fn contains(&self, digest: &Sha256Digest) -> io::Result<bool>
   Concurrency + dedup (hardened 2026-08-14): two concurrent put_blob calls with identical content converge on one blob. Windows rename semantics spelled out - rename onto an existing READ-ONLY destination ERRORS on Windows, so the dedup path is an explicit dance: check-exists -> full-hash-verify the existing blob -> on verified match treat as success and discard the temp file; on hash MISMATCH (corrupt existing bytes; content-addressing makes replacement always-safe) atomically heal: clear the read-only bit, temp+rename over the corrupt file, re-mark read-only, emit a diagnostic event - this closes the poisoned-blob-forever hole. put_blob exposes a pre-return commit hook so callers (MT-324 export seam) can commit their per-digest MT-326 lease BEFORE a dedup hit is reported as success - a dedup hit must never count as success ahead of its lease commit, or the sweeper can race the export. A crash mid-put leaves only a *.partial in cas/tmp which a startup sweep of files older than a threshold removes (plain remove_file on exact paths - no recursive delete, no --force semantics anywhere). No delete API for cas/sha256/ blobs exists in this MT at all; deletion authority arrives only with MT-326's lease-fenced GC.
4. Registry (base_image_registry.rs) + migration 03NN_base_image_registry.surql:
   SCHEMAFULL semantic field inventory for base_image_registry (
       base_image_id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
       image_digest TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (image_digest ~ '^sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$'),
       toolchain_id TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (length(btrim(toolchain_id)) > 0 AND toolchain_id !~ '\s'),
       image_format TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (image_format IN ('raw', 'qcow2')),
       size_bytes BIGINT NOT NULL CHECK (size_bytes > 0),
       cas_path_rel TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (cas_path_rel !~ '\s' AND cas_path_rel !~ '^[A-Za-z]:' AND left(cas_path_rel, 1) <> '/'),
       read_only BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT TRUE CHECK (read_only),
       owner_account_id UUID NOT NULL,
       actor_principal_id UUID NOT NULL,
       authenticated_session_id UUID NOT NULL,
       access_space_id UUID NOT NULL,
       workspace_id TEXT NOT NULL,
       created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
       CONSTRAINT uq_base_image_owner_toolchain UNIQUE (owner_account_id, toolchain_id),
       CONSTRAINT uq_base_image_owner_digest UNIQUE (owner_account_id, image_digest)
   );
   Define authenticated record-user table/field PERMISSIONS and re-authorize through ResourceBroker exact scope; the former 0365 registry insert is an audit anchor only. Rows are immutable-by-convention: registering a new toolchain version is a new toolchain_id row; there is no UPDATE path for image_digest.
   pub struct BaseImageRecord { base_image_id: Uuid, image_digest: Sha256Digest, toolchain_id: String, image_format: BaseImageFormat, size_bytes: i64, cas_path_rel: String, scope: StoredResourceScope, created_at: DateTime<Utc> }
   pub struct BaseImageRegistry { pool: SurrealDbClient, access: ResourceAccessContext }  // same durable-store shape as WorktreeVmRegistry::new_durable (worktree_vm_registry.rs lines 214-225)
   pub async fn register_base_image(&self, toolchain_id, digest, format, size_bytes) -> Result<BaseImageRecord, BaseImageError>  // insert stamped via ResourceAccessContext::write_scope / insert_columns (resource_scope.rs lines 849-852)
   pub async fn resolve_by_toolchain(&self, toolchain_id) -> Result<Option<BaseImageRecord>, BaseImageError>  // read filtered by authenticated SurrealQL permissions via authenticated record-user SurrealQL permissions plus ResourceBroker exact-scope authorization (resource_scope.rs line 798), rows re-authorized after deserialization via authorize_row (line 781)
5. Never-write-to-a-base enforcement (P4):
   - CAS blob files are chmod'd read-only after rename (best-effort on Windows host FS; the authoritative guard is the API surface).
   - No function in workspace_volumes:: opens a cas/sha256/ path with write access; a #[test] greps the module for OpenOptions::write(true) usage against cas blob paths as a tripwire, and a runtime test asserts that put_blob of different content NEVER lands on an existing digest path.
   - MT-322 records base->delta child edges in its binding table; the registry gains (in this MT) pub async fn has_children stub returning a typed NotYetTracked error so MT-322/MT-326 must wire it before any removal logic can compile against it.
6. RESOURCE PRIVACY NOTE (applies to every DW MT): base images, volumes, bundles, manifests, and GC visibility are account/Principal-scoped. Rows carry the five scope columns (resource_scope.rs OWNER_ACCOUNT_COLUMN..WORKSPACE_COLUMN, lines 854-858); reads are SQL-filtered via ResourceBroker authorization filter (line 798); derived artifacts inherit scope through ResourceScope::derive_from_sources (lines 193-228), which REFUSES mixed-scope derivation rather than computing a widening union (HBR-PRIV-004: 'a refusal is recoverable; a silent widening is a leak').

STEP-BY-STEP:
1. Read (post-WP-1-merge main) sandbox/cloud_hypervisor/adapter.rs config surface (CloudHypervisorConfig, lines ~394-520) and migrations/0365_worktree_vm_bindings.sql; confirm the next free migration sequence number.
2. Implement Sha256Digest with full parse/format/serde tests.
3. Implement runtime_root.rs with the repo-worktree rejection guard and env/config resolution order.
4. Implement HostCasStore: put_blob (temp+fsync+rename+dir-fsync+read-only), open_verified (streaming re-hash), contains, blob_path, startup partial-sweep.
5. Write migration 03NN_base_image_registry.surql; run it against the real development SurrealDB.
6. Implement BaseImageRegistry over SurrealDbClient + ResourceAccessContext with scope-stamped insert and scope-filtered reads.
7. Tests (Spec-Realism Gate: registry tests hit real SurrealDB via the crate's existing DB test harness; CAS tests hit the real filesystem under a scratch runtime root): atomic put, concurrent duplicate put convergence, corrupted-blob read rejection, crash-partial sweep, cross-account read denial, uq_base_image_owner_toolchain conflict surfaces as typed error, runtime-root-inside-worktree rejection.
8. Run proof targets under the scoped CARGO_TARGET_DIR; record measured output.
forbidden_paths: src/frontend/handshake_native/src/** and app/src/** (GUI belongs to MT-327)
session_worktrees/** and any repo worktree path (volume/CAS bytes live under the product runtime root only)
acceptance_criteria: AC-321-1: Sha256Digest parses/serializes only lowercase-hex 'sha256:'-prefixed digests; wrong prefix, wrong length, uppercase, and non-hex inputs are typed errors; serde round-trip proven.

AC-321-2: HostCasStore::put_blob streams to cas/tmp/<uuid>.partial, fsyncs the file, atomically renames into cas/sha256/<hex>, fsyncs the parent directory, then marks the blob read-only; a live test proves no partially-written blob is ever visible under cas/sha256/.

AC-321-3: Two concurrent put_blob calls with identical content converge to one blob without error; a crash-simulating test leaves only cas/tmp/*.partial which the startup sweep removes with plain remove_file (no recursive delete, no --force).

AC-321-4: open_verified re-hashes on read and a live test with a deliberately corrupted blob file yields CasError::IntegrityViolation naming expected and observed digests; no API returns unverified full blob content.

AC-321-5: A SurrealKit rollout defines SCHEMAFULL base_image_registry with full resource-scope fields, digest/format/no-spaces/relative-path ASSERT rules, owner/toolchain and owner/digest indexes, authenticated record-user PERMISSIONS, and real-SurrealDB proof.

AC-321-6: register_base_image stamps records through ResourceAccessContext; resolve_by_toolchain uses account-scoped SurrealQL plus record-user PERMISSIONS and re-authorizes through ResourceBroker; a live two-account test proves isolation.
AC-321-7: No code path in workspace_volumes opens a registered cas/sha256/ blob for write; blob files are read-only after commit; the write-to-base tripwire test fails closed.

AC-321-8: resolve_workspace_volumes_root refuses a root inside any git repo worktree with a typed error (live test), honors config > HANDSHAKE_RUNTIME_ROOT > platform-dir order, and every DB-stored path is relative with no spaces and no drive letter.

AC-321-9: Zero SQLite anywhere: no rusqlite/sqlite crate appears in Cargo.toml or the lockfile diff; grep proof target passes. No Docker/containerd/OCI-registry dependency is added; OCI/cacache are shape heuristics only.

AC-321-10: All proof commands run with the per-owner scoped CARGO_TARGET_DIR under ../Handshake_Artifacts/handshake-cargo-target/ and measured output is recorded; the implementer does not mark this MT COMPLETED (validator verdict authority only).

AC-321-11: put_blob's dedup-hit path full-hash-verifies the existing blob before reporting success and atomically heals a corrupt existing blob via clear-read-only + temp+rename + re-mark-read-only with a diagnostic event (live test with a pre-corrupted blob); the pre-return commit hook lets export leases commit before dedup success is reported (Windows rename-onto-read-only-destination error semantics handled explicitly).

implementation_notes: Field basis: P12 (cacache/sccache/Bazel CAS: /cas/<sha256> blobs, temp+rename atomic, integrity-verified reads), P11 (OCI descriptor digest shape as JSON heuristic), P4 (never write to a base with children), P7 (Docker reference model: read-only content-addressed base layers). All heuristics only - no cacache crate requirement, no Docker/containerd/OCI dependency.

House rules: all Rust; SurrealDB/EventLedger authority only, no SQLite; disk-agnostic relative paths with no spaces; volume/CAS bytes under the product runtime root, never inside repo worktrees; no --force deletes; implementer never marks COMPLETED.

Spec-Realism Gate: registry proofs run against real SurrealDB through the crate's existing DB test harness; CAS proofs touch the real filesystem under a scratch runtime root. Fixture-only proof is insufficient.

Deletion authority is deliberately absent from this MT: the only path that may ever unlink a cas/sha256/ blob is MT-326's lease-fenced GC, where un-promoted digests are structurally unreachable to the sweeper.

Resource privacy: mirror WorktreeVmRegistry::new_durable's SurrealDbClient + ResourceAccessContext shape (worktree_vm_registry.rs lines 214-225); scope stamping and filtering reuse resource_scope.rs primitives verbatim - do not hand-roll WHERE clauses.
Windows/WSL: CAS lives on the host-visible runtime root; ext4-image creation and WSL specifics are MT-322's concern - this MT is filesystem-portable Rust only.

gui_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Backend storage-foundation MT; the operator-facing volume/handoff surface is MT-327. CAS and registry activity is reconstructable from SurrealDB rows and the FR events MT-327 adds.

target_entries: Workspace volumes > Base images and CAS (runtime root resolution, HANDSHAKE_RUNTIME_ROOT, cas/sha256 layout, why bases are immutable)
Workspace volumes > Toolchain image registration (one row per toolchain version, account scoping)

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations.note: DW-family FR event kinds are introduced centrally in MT-327 (volume lifecycle/export/promotion/GC); this MT's registry writes are durable SurrealDB rows already reconstructable without FR. Record DEFERRED-to-MT-327.

Emit a diagnostic event on CAS integrity violation and on migration/registry write failure via the open diagnostic-event API if present in the implementing worktree; otherwise record DEFERRED-with-reason.
Short-lived synchronous file/SQL operations; liveness capture surviving a Handshake crash adds no evidence beyond the durable rows and partial-file sweep.

risk_if_missed: Without a content-addressed immutable base layer, MT-322 deltas would back onto mutable files (silent corruption of every child overlay), artifacts would be stored under mutable names with no integrity verification, and MT-326's GC would have no digest graph to compute reachability over - the entire handoff pipeline loses its integrity root.

risks: RISK-1: A torn or crashed put leaves a partial blob visible under cas/sha256/, and a later reader trusts the digest-named path without verification, propagating corrupt bytes into VM boot chains.
RISK-2: A code path (now or in a later MT) opens a base blob for write while qcow2 children back onto it, invalidating every child overlay silently (P4 failure mode).
RISK-3: The runtime root resolves inside a repo worktree (mis-set env), so multi-GB image bytes land in git status, get committed or reseed-deleted with the worktree.
RISK-4: Registry rows are written or read without resource-scope stamping/filtering, leaking one account's base-image inventory to another account's queries.
minimum_controls: CTRL-1 (RISK-1): temp+fsync+rename+dir-fsync write path with an observer-thread test proving no partial visibility; open_verified re-hashes every read and is the only full-read API.

CTRL-2 (RISK-2): read-only chmod after commit, no write-capable API over cas/sha256/, write-to-base tripwire test, and has_children seam reserved so MT-322/326 must wire child tracking before any removal logic exists.
CTRL-3 (RISK-3): resolve_workspace_volumes_root walks ancestors and fails closed on any .git ancestor; live test asserts the rejection; all DB paths are root-relative.
CTRL-4 (RISK-4): inserts go through ResourceAccessContext::insert_columns, reads through ResourceBroker authorization filter + authorize_row; two-account denial test is a named regression.

surrealdb_translation_v02_205.concurrency_rule: Translate advisory locks, SKIP LOCKED and row locks into SurrealDB transactions, durable lease/fencing records and conditional updates with equivalent tests.
